    Overview

    📚 What is this & why does it exist?

    Analogy — Library Shelf

    Imagine a multi-level library system. Your desk (L1 cache) has the few books you're currently reading — instant access. The room's bookshelf (L2 cache) holds more books but takes a short walk. The building's main library (L3 / memory) has everything but requires a trip downstairs. The replacement policy decides which book to remove from your desk when it's full. The prefetcher is a helpful librarian who notices your reading pattern and pre-fetches the next book before you ask. The MSHR is the checkout slip tracking which books you've requested but haven't arrived yet.

    The cache/ directory implements gem5's Classic memory system cache hierarchy. It provides:

    • BaseCache — abstract base managing tags, MSHRs, write queues, and port handling
    • Cache — coherent cache with snooping and flexible topologies
    • NoncoherentCache — simplified non-snooping cache
    • MSHR / WriteQueue — miss tracking and write coalescing
    • Replacement Policies — 12+ algorithms (LRU, FIFO, BIP, BRRIP, SHiP, TreePLRU, …)
    • Prefetchers — 14+ engines (Stride, BOP, AMPM, SPP, DCPT, ISB, …)
    • Tags — set-associative, fully-associative LRU, sector, compressed
    • Compressors — BDI, C-Pack, FPC, FPCD, FrequentValues

    Cache Request Processing Flow

    Click to expand 
    flowchart TD
    REQ["recvTimingReq()"]
    LOOKUP["Tag Lookup"]
    HIT{"Hit?"}
    RESP["Send Response"]
    MSHR_CHK{"MSHR exists?"}
    COALESCE["Coalesce into MSHR"]
    ALLOC["Allocate MSHR"]
    SEND["sendTimingReq() downstream"]
    FILL["handleFill()"]
    VICTIM["Select victim (RP)"]
    WB{"Dirty victim?"}
    WBACK["Writeback victim"]
    INSERT["Insert new block"]
    DEALLOC["Deallocate MSHR"]

    REQ --> LOOKUP
    LOOKUP --> HIT
    HIT -->|Yes| RESP
    HIT -->|No| MSHR_CHK
    MSHR_CHK -->|Yes| COALESCE
    MSHR_CHK -->|No| ALLOC
    ALLOC --> SEND
    SEND -->|Response arrives| FILL
    FILL --> VICTIM
    VICTIM --> WB
    WB -->|Yes| WBACK
    WB -->|No| INSERT
    WBACK --> INSERT
    INSERT --> DEALLOC
    DEALLOC --> RESP

    Replacement Policies

    All replacement policies live in cache/replacement_policies/ and extend a common base class. The cache invokes getVictim() to select an eviction candidate and touch() / reset() on access and insertion.

    PolicyFileAlgorithm
    LRURPlru_rp.hhLeast Recently Used — evicts the block with the oldest last-access timestamp.
    FIFORPfifo_rp.hhFirst-In First-Out — evicts the block inserted earliest, ignoring reuse.
    LFURPlfu_rp.hhLeast Frequently Used — evicts the block with the fewest accesses.
    MRURPmru_rp.hhMost Recently Used — evicts the most recently accessed block (thrash-resistant).
    RandomRPrandom_rp.hhRandom — evicts a randomly chosen block.
    BIPRPbip_rp.hhBimodal Insertion — inserts most blocks in LRU position; a small fraction in MRU (thrash protection).
    BRRIPRPbrrip_rp.hhBimodal Re-Reference Interval Prediction — extends BIP with multi-bit RRPV counters for finer granularity.
    SHiPRPship_rp.hhSignature-based Hit Predictor — uses PC-based signatures to predict reuse and set insertion priority.
    TreePLRURPtree_plru_rp.hhTree Pseudo-LRU — binary tree of 1-bit pointers; hardware-efficient LRU approximation.
    SecondChanceRPsecond_chance_rp.hhSecond Chance (Clock) — FIFO with a use bit; gives accessed blocks a second chance.
    DuelingRPdueling_rp.hhSet Dueling — dynamically selects between two constituent policies using tournament sampling.

    Prefetch Engines

    Prefetchers in cache/prefetch/ observe cache access patterns and issue speculative fetches. The Queued base maintains a FIFO of generated addresses, throttled by configurable degree.

    PrefetcherFileStrategy
    StridePrefetcherstride.hhDetects constant-stride access patterns per PC; Atomic and Timing Simple CPUs — gem5 Wiki" href="../../cpu_doc/simple/index.html">simple and effective for array traversals.
    BOPPrefetcherbop.hhBest Offset Prefetching — evaluates many candidate offsets and picks the best-performing one.
    AMPMPrefetcheraccess_map_pattern_matching.hhAccess Map Pattern Matching — tracks access bitmaps per page zone to detect complex patterns.
    SignaturePathPrefetchersignature_path.hhSPP — builds a signature table from delta history; follows lookahead paths for deep prefetching.
    SignaturePathPrefetcherV2signature_path_v2.hhSPP v2 with enhanced confidence and global accuracy feedback.
    DCPTPrefetcherdelta_correlating_prediction_tables.hhDelta Correlating Prediction Tables — correlates deltas between consecutive addresses.
    IndirectMemoryPrefetcherindirect_memory.hhHandles pointer-chasing patterns by tracking indirect memory accesses.
    IrregularStreamBufferirregular_stream_buffer.hhISB — maps structural addresses to temporal streams for irregular workloads.
    SBOOEPrefetchersbooe.hhSandbox-Based Optimal Offset Estimation — lightweight offset evaluation using sandbox.
    PIFPrefetcherpif.hhProactive Instruction Fetch — uses temporal address correlation for instruction streams.
    STeMSPrefetcherspatio_temporal_memory_streaming.hhSpatio-Temporal Memory Streaming — combines spatial and temporal patterns.
    SlimAMPMPrefetcherslim_ampm.hhLightweight AMPM variant with reduced storage.
    TaggedPrefetchertagged.hhSimple next-line prefetcher triggered on every cache access.

    MSHR & Write Buffer Handling

    MSHRs are the backbone of non-blocking cache operation. Each MSHR tracks one outstanding cache line fetch and coalesces all requests targeting the same block.

    MSHR Lifecycle

    Allocation — On a cache miss, MSHRQueue::allocate() creates an MSHR if one is available. If all MSHRs are busy, the cache blocks.
    Target coalescing — Subsequent misses to the same block are added as targets to the existing MSHR instead of issuing new downstream requests.
    Downstream fetch — The MSHR triggers a sendTimingReq() to the next cache level or memory controller.
    Response handling — When data returns, BaseCache::recvTimingResp() calls handleFill() to insert the block and service all coalesced targets.
    Deallocation — The MSHR is freed and the cache unblocks, allowing new misses to proceed.

    Write Buffer

    The WriteQueue holds pending writebacks and write-cleans. When a dirty block is evicted, a WriteQueueEntry is allocated. The write buffer has its own flow control and can cause the cache to block independently of MSHRs.

    // Simplified MSHR allocation in BaseCache::access()
MSHR *mshr = mshrQueue.findMatch(blk_addr);
if (mshr) {
    // Coalesce: add this request as a target
    mshr->allocateTarget(pkt, pkt->headerDelay, order++);
} else {
    // New miss: allocate MSHR and send downstream
    mshr = mshrQueue.allocate(blk_addr, blk_size, pkt, curTick(), order++);
    memSidePort.sendTimingReq(mshr->getTarget()->pkt);
}

    Tag Organization

    Tag stores determine how cache blocks are indexed and looked up. gem5 provides several implementations:

    Tag TypeFileOrganization
    BaseSetAssoctags/base_set_assoc.hhStandard set-associative with configurable indexing (modular, skewed, etc.).
    FALRUtags/fa_lru.hhFully-associative with LRU tracking. Useful for small filter caches or way-profiling studies.
    SectorTagstags/sector_tags.hhGroups of consecutive blocks share one tag. Reduces tag area for large caches.
    CompressedTagstags/compressed_tags.hhExtends sector tags: multiple compressed blocks can share a data entry if they fit.

    Component Deep Dives

    Replacement Policies

    12 algorithms from simple LRU/FIFO to advanced BRRIP and SHiP. Extends ReplacementPolicy::Base with getVictim(), reset(), touch(), and invalidate() hooks.

    replacement_policies/ · 12 policies · All extend Base

    Prefetch Algorithms

    14+ prefetchers from simple tagged/stride to sophisticated SPP, AMPM, and ISB. All hook into cache access notifications via BasePrefetcher::notify().

    prefetch/ · 14+ engines · Queued base class

    Compression

    Data compressors for compressed caches: BDI (Base-Delta-Immediate), C-Pack, FPC (Frequent Pattern Compression), FPCD, and FrequentValues. Compress blocks to fit more data in same area.

    compressors/ · 8+ algorithms · CompressedTags integration

    MSHR & Write Queue

    Non-blocking cache operation with configurable MSHR count, target coalescing, deferred targets for snoop handling, and separate write buffer for writebacks.

    mshr.hh, write_queue.hh · Core to cache performance

    Indexing Policies

    Set selection strategies: modular (traditional), skewed (XOR-based), and custom policies in tags/indexing_policies/.

    tags/indexing_policies/ · Pluggable indexing

    Partitioning Policies

    Cache partitioning for QoS: way partitioning and capacity allocation across requestors, managed by PartitionManager.

    tags/partitioning_policies/ · QoS integration

    Configuration Examples

    Classic cache hierarchy is configured through Python SimObjects. Key parameters:

    // Python configuration example (gem5 style)
// L1 Data Cache
system.cpu.dcache = Cache(
    size = '64kB',
    assoc = 8,
    tag_latency = 2,
    data_latency = 2,
    response_latency = 2,
    mshrs = 4,
    tgts_per_mshr = 20,
    write_buffers = 8,
    replacement_policy = LRURP(),
    prefetcher = StridePrefetcher(degree=4)
)

// L2 Shared Cache
system.l2cache = Cache(
    size = '2MB',
    assoc = 16,
    tag_latency = 10,
    data_latency = 10,
    response_latency = 10,
    mshrs = 20,
    tgts_per_mshr = 12,
    write_buffers = 16,
    clusivity = 'mostly_incl',
    replacement_policy = TreePLRURP(),
    prefetcher = BOPPrefetcher()
)
    ParameterTypeDescriptionTypical L1Typical L2
    sizeMemorySizeTotal cache capacity32-64 kB256 kB - 4 MB
    associntWays per set4-88-16
    tag_latencyCyclesTag array lookup latency1-28-20
    data_latencyCyclesData array read latency1-28-20
    mshrsintNumber of MSHRs (outstanding misses)4-816-32
    write_buffersintWrite buffer entries816-32
    clusivityenumInclusion policy—mostly_incl
    replacement_policySimObjectReplacement policy instanceLRURPTreePLRURP
    prefetcherSimObjectPrefetcher instanceStrideBOP/SPP
